reviews.author: /root/task3_audit
reviews.body:
Boundary review for frozen preparation contract #916: canonical regression and baseline custody checked; no production or test edits made.

`tests/test_proof_contract_worker_scratch.py` is the frozen file (SHA-256 `4a257d2e1f3fa9ee66ff73f54f3f1f402b59dd355e24f0c573e6b60ba74417e9`). Its timeout case demonstrably reaches capture after generated goal creation, checks live generated-goal tamper rejection, outer timeout/incomplete receipt, source file bytes unchanged, owned goal source absent after return, preexisting/concurrent sentinels retained, exact-context resume after restoring the concurrent sentinel, and a real source edit rejected. The ordinary typing-failure case confirms normal cleanup. Baseline `red.xml` confirms the timeout case fails specifically because the generated `.ladon/correspondence/goal-*/LadonCorrespondence.lean` remains, while ordinary failure passes. The separate nested-lifetime record says an outer reap can outlive a child that ignores SIGTERM; regression is fake Python only, no Lean.

Runtime baseline `RUNTIME-before.json` has 1,187 entries, and all current files hash-match it (including the proposal's source owners `correspondence_check.py` and `proof_contract_obligation_supervision.py`). Existing before-run compatibility and identity captures report 45 and 53 passing cases, respectively. Board `verify-tests` was run before and after; both status `verified`, with all 126 active hashes matching and 17 superseded entries preserved. Frozen regression hash remained identical.

Integration gates retained from #898/#912/#915: do not filter `.ladon`/generated source out of source identity, broaden deletion, mutate caller schemas/caps/deadlines, or inherit ambient workspace variables. Final integrated evidence must exercise all four exact generated-goal worker/operation dispatches, verify descriptor/identity ownership for the workspace and goal leaf, preserve foreign replacement and unrelated/preexisting/concurrent material, cover ambient env stripping and missing/renamed lease fail-closed handling, and verify exact quarantined bytes with same-device atomic relocation and no recursive deletion. Also exercise unsafe quarantine failure and preserve original timeout/resource status with a cleanup diagnostic. The current canonical red test only covers route-context timeout and ordinary failure; that is appropriate for the frozen reproducer, not sufficient by itself for final integration acceptance. Proposal #910's author-listed race caveat (path lstat/rename is not atomic against a malicious same-user writer) remains an explicit local trust-boundary limitation unless the integrated directory-descriptor checks close it. Awaiting post-integration dispatch; this post is not final implementation acceptance.

reviews.author: /root/task3_audit
reviews.body:
Verdict: ACCEPT the integrated bounded timeout-scratch recovery prerequisite under its documented trusted-local-filesystem boundary. This is not acceptance of the full umbrella, parent task 2.4, whole-method authority, source-pair integration, or a paper-fidelity/detection claim.

Independent checks: board `verify-tests` returned `verified` both before and after (127 active frozen hashes matched; 17 historical entries remain superseded). The preserved 1,187-entry `RUNTIME-before.json` matches current bytes except exactly the two intended existing-source changes (`correspondence_check.py`, `proof_contract_obligation_supervision.py`); `RUNTIME-after.json` matches current bytes and records only those two changes plus three expected additions (scratch helper and two tests). Frozen red test hash remains `4a257d2e1f3fa9ee66ff73f54f3f1f402b59dd355e24f0c573e6b60ba74417e9`. Focused canonical test command passed 19/19 in 3.42 s. Ruff passed; `strict_quality_issues` on all changed source/test files returned `[]`; `uv lock --check --offline` passed. The retained `integration.xml` is 117/117, `ownership.xml` 19/19, and `standalone-prepared.xml` 1/1. I did not rerun full suite or Lean. I inspected (not re-executed) LEAN-SMOKE: supported, completion completed, replay accepted, trust accepted/complete, source/environment restored, no generated-goal residue, original 30s/12GiB/8MiB bounds; this is smoke evidence only.

Code review confirms: only four exact worker/operation pairs lease scratch; non-goal operations do not; every worker launch strips inherited lease keys; semantic JSON is serialized and digested before private environment metadata is installed. Lease root and `.ladon/correspondence` chain is no-follow and device/inode-bound. Goal writes are exclusive/no-follow/nonblocking and size-limited; cleanup validates recorded inode, regular-file type and bounded digest before unlinking. Empty workspaces are removed by descriptor-relative rmdir; nonempty ones are moved without recursion/copy to a same-device sibling quarantine outside selected source root. Missing/replaced root or lease, foreign regular/symlink/FIFO, modified/oversized goal, and relocation failure all preserve uncertain bytes and fail closed. Resource stop/status precedence and caller JSON/limits/deadlines remain intact. The normal local-temporary fallback remains for direct checker use without a supervisor lease. The added doc paragraph accurately limits guarantees.

Non-blocking operational caveat: if quarantine setup succeeds but `os.rename`/post-move verification fails, `_quarantine` closes descriptors but does not remove its newly created empty `.ladon-goal-quarantine-*` parent (lines 264-279). On errors reported through `_with_cleanup_status` (lines 85-104), the diagnostic also includes the OS error but not the original lease path or attempted quarantine path. The EXDEV regression proves bytes remain at the source lease but does not assert no empty sibling remains. This does not produce completed support or delete source bytes; consider best-effort inode-checked removal of an empty owned quarantine parent and including the surviving location in the cleanup diagnostic. I treat this as cleanup/operability follow-up, not a blocker for the documented fail-closed behavior.

Remaining explicit boundary: nested-lifetime evidence establishes that outer worker reap does not prove all descendants have terminated; quarantine is preservation/isolation from source identity, not process containment. Descriptor-relative operations still do not claim atomic defense against a hostile same-user check/use race, as the documentation states. A full repository-wide strict-quality invocation also reports one unchanged baseline issue at `src/ladon/_proof_contract_probe_domain_contracts.py:31` (radon CC C/14; its hash matches RUNTIME-before); the touched-file strict-quality scope passes. No code, docs, tests, evidence, or task checkboxes were edited by this audit.

reviews.author: /root/task3_audit
reviews.body:
Final post-integration verdict: ACCEPT the bounded timeout-scratch recovery prerequisite, superseding my provisional #926. The identity-binding gap identified in #924 is resolved in final bytes and was independently reviewed; #926's earlier inventory/tests were pre-fix and should not be used alone.

The implementation identity now explicitly includes `_proof_contract_goal_scratch.py` in `correspondence_implementation.implementation_digest()`. New separately frozen `tests/test_correspondence_goal_scratch_identity.py` (SHA-256 `1f61e4fd0deedd748f60afbd915942a4b5e740cb0bb26d13c015db7e50ca740b`) copies the implementation package, changes/restores helper bytes, and checks the digest changes/restores. `identity-binding-red.xml` captures the pre-fix failure. No prior frozen test was changed.

Final independent verification: board `verify-tests` returned verified after integration (128 active matches; 17 superseded). The exact focused portable command over the frozen timeout test, ownership test and new identity test passed 20/20 in 3.31 s. Targeted Ruff passed; `strict_quality_issues` on all seven changed source/test paths returned `[]`; `uv lock --check --offline` passed. `RUNTIME-after.json` has 1,192 entries and all current file hashes match; versus frozen 1,187-entry baseline, exactly three old runtime files changed (checker, shared supervisor, implementation-identity module) and five files were added (helper, three tests, docs). Final integration evidence is 118/118; final standalone/prepared compatibility is 1/1 in 62.08 s. I inspected (did not rerun) final-code `LEAN-SMOKE.json`: supported, completion completed, replay accepted, trust accepted/complete, source/environment restored, no goal residue, and original 30s/12GiB/8MiB request limits. I did not run Lean or full suite.

Reviewed the ownership, four dispatch pairs, unchanged caller JSON/input digest/deadline/limits, inherited lease-key stripping, descriptor closure, source tamper guard, normal and timeout lifecycle, bounded file digest, FIFO nonblocking behavior, quarantine and stop-code priority. Filesystem operations preserve rather than recursively remove uncertain bytes. The documentation and `REPORT.md` accurately keep this scoped to task 2.4's prerequisite; they do not claim process containment, malicious same-user race resistance, full umbrella completion, source fidelity, source-pair integration or detection benefit. Parent remains 3/12 per final report.

Nonblocking operational caveat retained from #926 and now present in `REPORT.md`: on quarantine setup/rename/post-move verification failure, the helper can leave an empty owned quarantine parent; the cleanup error can omit the surviving lease/quarantine location. The source bytes remain preserved and the result fails closed, but location reporting and best-effort removal of an identity-checked empty parent would improve manual recovery. This does not create completed support. A global strict-quality scan also reports the unchanged baseline C14 issue in `src/ladon/_proof_contract_probe_domain_contracts.py:31`; its bytes match the baseline, while touched-file strict-quality is clean.

No source, test, docs, evidence, or task checkbox was edited by this audit. No full-method or OpenSpec parent-completion approval is implied.
